Continuous Queries

1. What are Continuous Queries?
  • A continuous query allows you to receive real-time notifications whenever data in a cache changes (insert, update, delete);
  • The listener runs on the client that registered the query;
  • Optional: a remote filter runs on the server nodes to filter events before sending them to the client — this reduces network traffic;
2. Basic Continuous Query
  • ContinuousQuery<Integer, String> query = new ContinuousQuery<>();

// Local listener — runs on the client
query.setLocalListener(events -> {
    for (CacheEntryEvent<? extends Integer, ? extends String> e : events) {
        System.out.printf("Key: %d, Old: %s, New: %s, Type: %s%n",
            e.getKey(), e.getOldValue(), e.getValue(), e.getEventType());
    }
});

// Register — cursor stays open and receives events
QueryCursor<Cache.Entry<Integer, String>> cursor = cache.query(query);

// When done, close the cursor to stop receiving events
cursor.close();
3. Remote Filter
  • A remote filter runs on server nodes to decide which events to forward to the client: 
    query.setRemoteFilterFactory(() -> event -> {
    // Only notify for values that start with "VIP"
    return event.getValue().toString().startsWith("VIP");
});
  • This prevents sending every single change over the network — only matching events reach the client;
4. Initial Query
  • You can combine a continuous query with an initial query — first get a snapshot of current data, then receive live updates: 
    query.setInitialQuery(new ScanQuery<>()); // or SqlFieldsQuery

QueryCursor<Cache.Entry<Integer, String>> cursor = cache.query(query);

// Iterate over initial results
for (Cache.Entry<Integer, String> entry : cursor) {
    System.out.println("Initial: " + entry.getKey() + " = " + entry.getValue());
}

// After iteration, continuous events flow to the local listener
5. Use Cases
  • Real-time dashboards — update UI when data changes;
  • Event-driven architectures — trigger downstream processing on data mutations;
  • Cache synchronization — keep a local data structure in sync with the distributed cache;
  • Auditing — log all changes to a specific cache;
